title: ASRock Industrial AI Box-A395 Review: Taking Strix Halo to Work
gist: First half of a ServeTheHome review of ASRock Industrial's barebones Ryzen AI Max+ 395 tower, which the reviewer frames as a portable industrial mini-PC rather than an AI workstation, covering its specs, ports (10GbE plus 2.5GbE) and external design.

themes.theme: Strix Halo demand from local AI

insights.claim: Demand for local AI inference has exploded, and AMD's Ryzen AI Max (Strix Halo) chips have ended up in a far wilder product ecosystem than AMD expected, mainly as mini-PCs rather than laptops.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Local always-on AI boxes are a real demand pocket for AMD's high-end integrated silicon; watch partner design wins beyond laptops.

insights.claim: Ryzen AI Max mini-PCs are attractive as always-on local AI boxes for running agents and models, which is why the desktop mini-PC category has grown quickly while laptop designs have been scarcer.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Edge agent hosting is pulling demand toward unified-memory APUs instead of discrete GPUs.

insights.claim: The ASRock Industrial AI Box-A395 pairs a Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (16C/32T, Radeon 8060S with 40 CUs) with 128GB soldered LPDDR5X-8000, two empty M.2 PCIe Gen4 x4 slots and a 400W internal PSU in a 200x100x232 mm, 2.8kg barebones tower.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Soldered 128GB memory fixes the model size ceiling for local inference on this box.

insights.claim: The reviewer judges ASRock's 'AI workstation' marketing too optimistic and frames the A395 as a portable Ryzen AI Max system for industrial or unattended environments.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Expect this product to sell on ruggedness and headless deployment, not workstation performance.

insights.claim: The A395 is built as a standing mini-ITX-style case with an ATX I/O shield and integrated power supply, not a custom chassis designed around the Ryzen AI Max+ processor.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Reusing standard form factors lowers vendor design cost for Strix Halo systems.

insights.claim: The A395 runs on any standard C13 power cable via an internal PSU, making it self-contained for headless industrial deployments.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Removes the external brick, a practical edge for field and always-on use.

insights.claim: The A395 puts only two USB 2.x 480Mbps ports on top and no high-speed ports on the front, signalling industrial rather than workstation design intent.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Buyers needing front high-speed I/O should look elsewhere.

insights.claim: The A395 includes a 10GbE port (Marvell AQC113) plus a 2.5GbE port (Realtek RTL8125BG); the reviewer notes 10GbE has been rarer than desired on Ryzen AI Max+ 395 systems, and Framework Desktop ships with only one 5GbE or 2.5GbE port.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: 10GbE inclusion is a differentiator for clustering or NAS-fed local AI nodes.

insights.claim: Strix Halo silicon natively supports two 40Gbps USB-C ports and the iGPU can drive up to four monitors, with two HDMI 2.1 ports plus DisplayPort over USB-C on the A395.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Using USB-C for displays consumes the fastest USB ports, a trade-off for expansion.
